narrative.summary: The Central African Republic has no published AI-specific law, strategy or guidance. Its only AI-relevant national instrument is the 2024 personal data protection law (Law 24.001), which defines profiling and gives people the right to know and contest the logic of automated decisions with legal effects. A national AI strategy for 2024-2028 has been mentioned by a minister but not published. Several government websites, including the official gazette, the government portal and the digital ministry, could not be accessed during this review.
lead_institutions: Ministry of Posts, Telecommunications and Digital Economy
narrative.review_notes: This review was carried out on 12 October 2026, but the official gazette, the government portal, the digital ministry and parliament websites could not be accessed, so only one document could be read. The Central African Republic is marked for a later retry.

instruments.official_title: Loi n° 24.001 portant protection des données à caractère personnel
instruments.english_title: Law No. 24.001 on the Protection of Personal Data
instruments.issuing_authority: National Assembly (adopted) and President of the Republic (promulgated)
instruments.current_status: Promulgated 25 January 2024; Art. 58 states it takes effect from its promulgation and is to be published in the Journal officiel (gazette reference not found online). Art. 57 gave the ministry in charge of the digital economy, posts and telecommunications 12 months to set up the data protection agency, with the ministry exercising its functions in the meantime; whether the agency has been established could not be confirmed from an official source. Copy published on the website of the telecom regulator ARCEP-RCA.
instruments.summary: The Central African Republic's first general personal data protection law, applying to processing by controllers or processors established in the country and to processing that produces effects there, including public security and defence subject to specific derogations. It sets core processing principles, cross-border transfer rules, prior declaration/authorisation formalities, data subject rights and sanctions, and places compliance under an independent administrative data protection agency. It defines profiling and, under Art. 30, gives individuals a right to information allowing them to know and contest the logic of automated processing where a decision based on it produces legal effects on them.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: General data protection law governing personal data used in AI training and use; includes a profiling definition and a right to know and contest the logic of automated decisions (Art. 30).
